title: Metallogenic quantum criticality: Fermi surface nucleation at transitions between gapped phases
abstract: Continuous quantum phase transitions in interacting many-body systems exhibit universal phenomena that are largely independent of microscopic details. An organizing principle distilled from canonical examples such as the magnetic transition in Ising models is that the low-energy physics of transitions between gapped phases is governed by scale-invariant quantum field theories with gapless degrees of freedom at isolated points in momentum space. In this paper, we show that this principle can fail in a radical way: an entire gapless Fermi surface can emerge at a quantum critical point separating two fully gapped insulators. These exotic phase transitions are dubbed \textit{metallogenic quantum critical points} (MGQCP). We construct a controlled family of effective field theories for MGQCPs between distinct fractional Chern insulators and propose a periodically modulated quantum Hall bilayer as a minimal microscopic setting. The critical theory exhibits an unusual mixture of physical signatures: while transport and compressibility follow scaling laws compatible with a conformal field theory, the electron spectral function develops a power-law non-analyticity at the Fermi momentum, characteristic of non-Fermi-liquid metals. We discuss how the concept of MGQCP may shed new light on critical phenomena in moire materials with tunable Chern bands. More generally, our results point to a broader class of quantum critical phenomena in which extended manifolds of gapless excitations emerge in momentum space despite being absent in both neighboring phases.
summary: This theoretical work introduces Metallogenic Quantum Critical Points (MGQCPs), where a Fermi surface unexpectedly emerges at a quantum phase transition between two gapped insulating states. By constructing effective field theories for these transitions, the authors show that the critical point exhibits non-Fermi liquid behavior, challenging established paradigms of quantum criticality.
main_problem: The paper investigates a radical failure of standard quantum critical point theory, where an entire gapless Fermi surface can emerge at a quantum critical point separating two fully gapped insulating phases.
main_result: These exotic transitions, called Metallogenic Quantum Critical Points (MGQCPs), are characterized by a critical Fermi surface and exhibit non-Fermi liquid spectral function signatures, despite the neighboring phases being gapped.
method: The authors construct controlled effective field theories by combining analyses of fermionic composite fermion fluctuations with critical bosonic field theories (like QED3) using parton constructions and mean-field theory.
model_or_system: The minimal model is a quantum Hall bilayer system transitioning between two distinct Fractional Chern Insulators (FCIs). The physics is described by coupling fermionic partons to background gauge fields arising from the bosonic transition.
key_observables: Fermi surface existence, spectral function non-analyticity, resistivity scaling laws, and topological invariants (Hall conductivities, central charges).

main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field approximations for the bosonic phases and the use of parton constructions to decouple the low-energy physics.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the phase diagram showing the emergence of an NFL metal at the FCI transition, and diagrams detail the underlying QED3 sector and the role of gauge fluctuations.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the general principle, constructing the effective Lagrangian by coupling fermionic and bosonic sectors, analyzing the stability of pairing instabilities via RG flow, and finally confirming the MGQCP nature through specific FCI transitions.
why_interesting: The concept of MGQCPs provides a powerful, non-standard framework for understanding critical points in strongly correlated electron systems, particularly those involving topological insulators and moire heterostructures.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic phase diagram in which a critical non- Fermi liquid (NFL) metal with a gapless Fermi surface emerges at the phase transition between two fully gapped frac- tional Chern insulators (FCIs) with Abelian anyons ai.

FIG. 2. Physical mechanism for a metallogenic quantum crit- ical point. In the vicinity of the critical point, the system decomposes into a QED3 (2+1D quantum electrodynamics) sector and two Fermi surfaces f1, f2 coupled to the same set of emergent U(1) gauge fields. For either sign of the Dirac mass in QED3, gauge fluctuations induce a pairing instability between f1 and f2, leading to fully gapped phases. Precisely at criticality, gapless Dirac fermions modify the gauge field dynamics and stabilize the Fermi surfaces.

FIG. 3. Finite temperature crossover near the MGQCP. An ϵ- expansion estimate of the correlation length exponent ν ≈1.5 explains the shape of the crossover curves. The critical NFL and the gCFLs all have gapless Fermi surfaces. One crucial difference is that the electron is gapped in the gCFLs but gapless and strongly damped in the critical NFL.
